correctness.rationale: From polygonal support faces, for each edge E_j=[v_j,v_{j+1}] the antipodal support face is v_{j+m+1}; the edge-normal middle set is (E_j+v_{j+m+1})/2=[c_j,c_{j+m+1}]. All other middle sets are singleton endpoints, so Schneider’s polygon description identifies the hull A_P as conv{c_j}. Distinct rotated c_j have radius R sin(π/(2n)) and are exposed in A_P; Schneider 2015 Lemma 6 makes each a convexity point. Conversely the continuous q_z(φ)=⟨z,u(φ)⟩−[h_P(u)−h_P(−u)]/2 is π-antiperiodic, so has a zero. Schneider Lemma 2 demands z lie in the middle set at EVERY zero for convexity. If z is not any endpoint c_j, such a zero with z in a relative interior of [c_j,c_{j+m+1}] is a strict local extremum by the one-sided support derivatives. Yet antiperiodicity from a maximum to its shifted minimum forces a sign-changing zero in between, where z cannot lie in an edge middle segment or singleton, contradiction. Verified index formula and radius; finite n=3..101 checker is only corroboration.
residual_risks: Requires absence of parallel edges; holds for regular odd polygons, not regular even polygons.
Key one-sided derivative sign relies on z being interior to an exposed middle segment; corners separately exhausted.

value.rationale: Fills a natural finite-cardinality problem in the exact setting introduced by Schneider: gives canonical convex bodies with each odd finite number n≥3 of convexity points, and computes their full geometric locus and radius. The exact upper bound is nontrivial because exposed hedgehog vertices supply merely sufficient convexity points, while a middle segment could a priori hold extras. This is a motivated complete classification for a recognizable symmetry family, not an arbitrary low-n enumeration.
residual_risks: No result for even n or uniqueness/possible finite cardinalities among general planar convex bodies.

final_claim: For every regular odd Euclidean n-gon (n=2m+1≥3), its reflection-convexity points z such that P∪(2z−P) is convex are exactly the n longest-diagonal midpoints c_j=(v_j+v_{j+m+1})/2, themselves the vertices of a concentric regular n-gon of radius R sin(π/(2n)).
limitations: Exactly regular odd polygons, not arbitrary polygons or even regular polygons.
